headline: Bengaluru pothole designated as 'temporary public swimming pool' to meet infrastructure repair deadline
body:
Q: The Gunjur-Varthur road repair project has taken a fascinating turn; can you explain why the local civic body decided to fill the giant craters with chlorinated water instead of asphalt?

A: Look, we were under strict orders to fix the road by Friday. After realizing the contractor had left for a two-week trekking trip, we realized that an asphalt patch would take three days to set. By simply adding a filtration pump and a diving board, we transformed a six-foot-deep crater into a ‘Community Aquatic Center’ that provides immediate recreational value to the neighborhood.

Q: Isn't this just a way to avoid fixing the actual road surface?

A: Not at all, it’s a pivot to wellness. Residents were complaining about the commute, but now they are complaining about the lack of lanes for their morning laps. We have even hired a local lifeguard who stands in the middle of the road with a whistle to ensure no one tries to drive their sedan into the deep end.

Q: What happens if a car accidentally falls into the new aquatic center?

A: We call that a 'synchronized swimming event' and bill the insurance company for the pool maintenance. It’s actually quite efficient; the car gets a thorough wash while the driver learns a valuable lesson about infrastructure-adjacent sports.
caption: New infrastructure initiative turns commutes into cardio sessions. Would you take a dip in your local crater? 🏊‍♂️🚗 #BengaluruTraffic #RoadsToPools #GunjurVarthur #CivicInnovation (satire)
